questions.q:
In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option.

The United Nations has (A)/ declared Finland as (B)/ a world's happiest nation (C)/ for the third consecutive year. (D)
questions.s:
Part C has an error.

'Happiest' is a superlative degree adjective. We always use the definitive article 'the' with a superlative degree adjective. So, the indefinite article 'a' should be replaced with the definite article 'the' to rectify the given sentence.

Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

The correct sentence is: The United Nations has declared Finland as the world's happiest nation for the third consecutive year.

questions.q: (a) The faster he completes /(b) the work given to /(c) him, the largest will be his profit. /(d) No error.
This is (a) / a very unique (b) / experience. (c) / No error (d)
questions.s: The error is in part (b). 'Unique' is absolute; 'very unique' is incorrect. Correct form is 'a unique experience.' Answer: (b). 'Unique' absolute hai, 'very unique' galat hai. Sahi form hai 'a unique experience.' Jawab: (b).

questions.q: The second option had lesser impact on the environment compared to the first.
o: lesser impact on the environment
questions.s:
"less" is the appropriate term to compare the impact of the second option with that of the first.

The corrected sentence would be: "The second option had less impact on the environment compared to the first."

  • “Lesser” is used as a comparative adjective before a noun in some formal contexts but is usually used in phrases like “of lesser importance”.

  • When comparing quantities or degree in general, “less” is correct.

questions.q:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

The project was completed / more quicker / than expected.
questions.s: This is an error of double comparison. "Quicker" is already a comparative form of "quick," so adding "more" creates redundancy. It should be either "more quickly" or simply "quicker." Since "quicker" already indicates comparison, "more" is unnecessary and incorrect.

Anamika is the smartest and _____ of all students.
questions.s:
Two adjectives which refer to the same noun or pronoun joined by conjunction must be in the same degree of comparison. So, the blank will be filled by a superlative form of adjective. Hence, (c) is the correct answer.

The final sentence will be: Anamika is the smartest and kindest of all students.

questions.q: Select the option that changes the degree of comparison in the given sentence from superlative to positive without changing the meaning of the sentence.
o: Kalpana Ahuja is as tallest as other girls of the colony.
Many girls in the colony are taller than Kalpana Ahuja.
No other girl in the colony is as tall as Kalpana Ahuja.
No other girl in the colony is as taller as Kalpana Ahuja.
questions.s:
Answer: No other girl in the colony is as tall as Kalpana Ahuja.

Explanation:

  • The original sentence uses the superlative form: "the tallest girl."

  • The correct positive degree form that keeps the same meaning is:
    "No other girl in the colony is as tall as Kalpana Ahuja."

  • This compares Kalpana’s height with others without using the superlative.

Other options:

  • "Kalpana Ahuja is as tallest as other girls" – incorrect grammar

  • "Many girls in the colony are taller than Kalpana Ahuja" – opposite meaning

  • "No other girl in the colony is as taller as Kalpana Ahuja" – incorrect grammar

Correct sentence:
"No other girl in the colony is as tall as Kalpana Ahuja."
